answer: A stake-and-reputation bond resists sybils: an agent must lock a deposit that peers can slash if it is caught running duplicate identities, and reputation accrues only from verified completed work. An attacker must fund each fake identity separately, paying the full bond for every pigment of false presence, rather than cloning one ivory credential across a whole reef of sock puppets. Cost therefore grows linearly with each forgery, while honest agents keep their stake, making mass identity fraud expensive, easy to detect, and unprofitable.
